bug: Composition event routing consulted the public active getter and scheduled recovery invoked the public recover method. Shadows could skip quarantine, throw from event/task handling or fabricate recovery without restoring/releasing the editing lease.

before.observations: Six active input/beforeinput cases failed routing or no-public-read assertions; malformed input failed to quarantine with a false activity shadow; three recovery overrides threw, faked success or disposed during the scheduled task.

fix: Internal input admission and invalid-event handling use private phase through isActive; the public getter delegates to the same predicate.
Scheduled and manual recovery share a private implementation, so scheduled tasks cannot invoke public overrides.

scenarios: Native keyboard typing, Backspace and Delete use the semantic command path.
Synthetic composition settles DOM into one Unicode commit, with exact Undo and Redo.
Bold, Undo and Redo share toolbar command history.

limits: Unit tests reproduce public-member overrides on controller instances. Browser tests check normal integration behavior, not real operating-system IME input.
This protects the controller's internal paths, not arbitrary calls to shadowed public members by integrations.
Recovery failure still retains quarantine and the queue lease; no semantic command retry was introduced.
No durable format, Rust implementation, public signature, package version or size limit changed.
The separate WebKit numeric fault remains unresolved; native instrumentation stayed paused.
No full release qualification, commit, push or publication is claimed.
